headline: GH secretagogues
punch: Day one is not day thirty.

headline: Ipamorelin, GHRP-2, hexarelin
body: So instead of injecting growth hormone itself, these compounds make your own pituitary release it. The pitch you will hear is that this gives you a natural pulse instead of a flat depot sitting under your skin, and based on everything in the pulsatility post, that pitch is mechanically correct. Pulses are what the growth plate responds to. | The problem is the second half of the story, which almost nobody puts in their protocol because it only shows up if you keep measuring past the first week.
punch: The pitch is real. So is the catch.

headline: What happens over thirty days?
body: They ran GHRP-2 as a **continuous 30-day subcutaneous infusion** in healthy older men and women, and measured pulsatile GH secretion at three points: day 1, day 14 and day 30. That design is the important part, because most studies stop before day 14 and never see what happens next. | On day 1 the infusion stimulated pulsatile GH secretion by **more than 3 fold** versus baseline. Real, significant, P < 0.001. Exactly what the marketing says it does.
punch: Day one, it worked exactly as advertised.

headline: Day 14 is not day 1
body: By day 14 and again at day 30, the same infusion in the same people was driving GH by **more than 1.8 fold**. Still statistically significant, still genuinely working, and roughly 40 percent smaller than it was two weeks earlier. | What this means is that nothing changed except time. Same compound, same dose, same subjects, same delivery. The axis simply stopped answering as loudly. Any protocol built on week one numbers is built on a number that does not hold.
punch: ==3 fold on day 1. 1.8 fold by day 14.==

headline: This was already known
body: The same paper states it directly: acute administration of a high dose of GHRP **down-regulates homologous responsiveness of the somatotropic axis in all mammalian species studied**. | Every species anyone has tested this in. That is not a side effect of bad dosing or a quality problem with the peptide. It is a documented property of how the receptor behaves when you keep agonising it, and it was in the literature before most of these compounds were being sold.
punch: _The axis adapts. In every species tested._

headline: The honest version
subhead: WHAT THEY DO AND DO NOT DO
body: What they genuinely do is produce pulsatile GH, which from the Isgaard and Bick data is the pattern the growth plate and muscle actually respond to. That is a real mechanistic advantage over a flat subcutaneous GH depot and it should not be dismissed. | What they do not do is hold the day one magnitude. So the mechanism is right and the size of the effect shrinks by about 40 percent within two weeks and then stabilises there.

headline: What they did to bone
body: Svensson gave ipamorelin and GHRP-6 to rats and measured the skeleton directly rather than just measuring hormones. Bone mineral content rose and cross-sectional bone area rose. | But the **volumetric bone density was unchanged**. What this means is that the increase in total mineral came from the bones getting physically bigger, not from the existing bone getting denser. Which is exactly what you would predict if the effect is running through the growth plate rather than through remodelling.

headline: When should you judge one?
body: A secretagogue gives you the right delivery pattern at a magnitude that shrinks. So judge one at week four, never at week one, because week one flatters it by roughly 40 percent and that gap is a receptor property rather than anything you can dose around. | And expect the bone effect to show up as size rather than density, because size is what was actually measured.
